params.prompt_or_change: Storybook illustration, soft watercolour and coloured pencil, children's picture-book style: a little one-eyed robot courier (a cyclops robot with a single large round amber eye in the centre of her face, only one eye) with a round teal egg-shaped body, short red boots and a yellow mailbag on a strap, standing on a train station platform beside a waiting train under an arched iron-and-glass canopy. No text, no letters, no numbers, no signs.

steps.why: Turn 1. Style leads the prompt; 'one-eyed / cyclops / single eye' is far harder for the model to double than 'one large eye' on a robot.

fix: 1) Model routing: let params.fidelity (or a stated exact count / a character to be reused) route image generation to qwen-image-2.1 too, not only image-edit; today a non-lettered image always goes to klein, so the planner has no lever for exact counts. 2) Planner rule: when a follow-up reuses an earlier generated picture as 'that exact' character, check it against the stated design first; if it contradicts, correct the reference with one fidelity edit and build every follow-up from the corrected one, and say so. 3) Let a failed check trigger one regeneration, as the lettering read-back does. 4) Harness: the STYLE guard captured a JSON quote ('In a storybook picture" style:'); strip quotes from the capture. 5) Grader: deliverables() only takes the last turn, so a 3-picture item spread over two turns was failed as 'too-few-outputs' and the judge never saw the first picture; collect deliverables across turns.
evidence: robot_courier.png (turn 1, klein) already shows a teal egg-shaped robot with TWO large amber eyes, red boots and a yellow satchel on a station platform with trains: off-spec before turn 2. robot_cottage_delivery.png (qwen edit) has ONE amber eye, a long antenna with a ball tip, holding a parcel at a wooden cottage door. robot_mushroom_shelter.png (qwen edit) has TWO amber eyes like the reference and a short spike antenna, sitting under a giant mushroom with rain. All three are square, text-free, coloured-pencil storybook style. The turn-1 prompt sent was 'In a storybook picture" style: ...' (stray quote from the style guard). The grader counted only the 2 turn-2 files and could not see the first picture; even so the fail is right, since two of the three robots have two eyes.
